inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-flows, USD risk-free rate + ERP. 9.5% reflects a cyclical, capital-intensive oil & gas E&P/LNG producer -- above a stable US tech default (10.5%... actually below, cyclicals in this folder run ~9%) but above a regulated-utility rate; Santos carries investment-grade ratings (Baa3 positive Moody's, BBB S&P/Fitch) and ~28% gearing, tempering the premium a pure-play smaller E&P would need. Risk (commodity cyclicality, PNG country risk, execution risk on Papua LNG) is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked again as a WACC premium (adaptations file 7f) -- WACC is IDENTICAL across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): leases as debt. Lease liabilities (US$1,464m at 30-Jun-2026, up from $821m FY2024 on recognition of the Barossa FPSO lease) sit inside the balance-sheet total_debt figure used for net_debt, and are NOT deducted a second time from the flows. Reported free_cash_flow = operating_cash_flow - capex ties exactly across FY2023-FY2025 (verified), confirming lease principal (a financing outflow under IFRS 16) is already excluded from OCF and is not being double-subtracted. Management's own 'Net debt' KPI (FY2025: $5,764m) is defined inclusive of lease liabilities and net of hedges/swaps -- the DB's total_debt-minus-cash figure ($5,818m FY2025 balance date, $6,223m at 30-Jun-2026) is consistent with that definition to within hedge/swap noise.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial. NCI reported only in FY2024 ($40m); FY2025 shows nil. No consolidated subsidiary carries a persistent large minority stake (PNG LNG, GLNG, Darwin LNG are proportionately/equity accounted per Santos's working interest, not consolidated-with-NCI structures at the group level for the disclosed periods). No adjustment made; flagged for re-check if a future filing shows a material NCI line.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, MID-CYCLE basis (dcf-methods SKILL.md routing: 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' row -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Santos is a classic commodity-cyclical E&P/LNG producer -- reported FCF swings from -$610m (FY2015, oil crash) to $2,851m (FY2022, post-Ukraine price spike) to $449m (FY2024, trough of the Barossa/Pikka capex supercycle) to $757m (FY2025). The FY2025 owner-FCF base ($731m) is NOT extrapolated forward with a flat growth rate -- it is capex-depressed (FY2025 capex $2,056m = 40% of revenue, guided to stay ~$1.95-2.15bn in FY2026) by the tail of the Barossa+Pikka construction cycle, which per management's own commentary is 'now behind the company' as both assets reached production in 2025-2026. The base case therefore builds forward from components (EBITDA margin, capex%, D&A%, cash tax rate paths) reflecting: (1) full-year Barossa+Pikka volume contribution and the guided 25-30% production growth by 2027 vs 2024, (2) capex tapering from the FY2025/26 construction-tail level toward a lower sustaining level as major projects complete, offset from ~2028 by Papua LNG construction capex (FID targeted Q4 2026, Santos ~21% stake, ~US$14bn total multi-partner spend), and (3) EBITDA margin held flat to the FY2022-2025 actual range of 66-67% (NOT the FY2021 pre-cost-program 55%), since Santos's own disclosed unit production cost has fallen from $8.04/boe (2020) to $6.78/boe (FY2025) and margin has proven stable through the commodity cycle -- revenue swings with price/volume, not margin. No oil/LNG price-deck re-rating is assumed: current spot Brent (~$100-108/bbl late-Sep-2026, WTI ~$93/bbl) sits well above Santos's guided $45-50/bbl all-in FCF breakeven, but base-case revenue growth is volume-driven only, treating today's elevated price level as cyclically above mid-cycle rather than the new normal -- this is the conservative, non-re-rating convention this folder applies to cyclicals. SBC is small (~0.4-0.7% of revenue every year) and expensed; share count held FLAT (fully diluted 3,257m shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026; SBC dilution is immaterial for this company, buybacks were $316m FY2023 only, zero since as the balance sheet absorbed Barossa/Pikka capex). Net debt taken at the 30-Jun-2026 balance date (post Barossa FPSO lease recognition) rather than the FY2025 year-end figure, since it is the latest available. Currency: filings and all flows are in USD (confirmed FY2015 annual and every filing since; Santos switched functional/presentation currency to USD from FY2016). Quote is in AUD on the ASX -- current_price, intrinsic_value and weighted_iv are all reported in AUD (quote currency) via fx_rate 0.7019 (AUDUSD, Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-25); a currency-suffixed USD twin is also emitted. The 2025 XRG/ADNOC-led consortium takeover approach (~US$5.76/share indicative, ~A$8.89 implied at the time's FX) was formally withdrawn 17-Sep-2025 and is not live -- no deal-completes/deal-breaks scenario weighting is applied; it is noted in valuation_philosophy as context for why the market has historically assigned a strategic-scarcity premium, and because the current price sits near/above the house intrinsic value it is a relevant explanation for any residual premium versus a pure DCF.
inputs.fx_note: Filings/flows are USD (inputs.currency); ASX quote is AUD (inputs.quote_currency). fx_rate is quote-currency-per-model-currency (USD->AUD), matching the engine convention (scripts/dcf_engine.py multiplies the USD per-share value by fx_rate to get AUD; verified against SMI.NZ's AUD/NZD 1.2123 = '1 AUD = 1.2123 NZD' precedent). AUDUSD=X on Yahoo Finance quoted 0.7019 (1 AUD = 0.7019 USD) as of 2026-09-25T05:16Z; fx_rate = 1/0.7019 = 1.4247 (1 USD = 1.4247 AUD). No STO.AX dual listing exists for a direct parity check; cross-checked instead against the ASX quote itself: USD intrinsic_value_usd x fx_rate must reproduce the AUD intrinsic_value, and the AUD figure must be of the same order of magnitude as the AUD quote (8.595) -- confirmed after the fix (base ~5.69 USD x 1.4247 ~= 8.11 AUD, close to the live quote).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All CAGRs here are noise from the commodity cycle and are NOT used to set the projection -- flagged per method, not applied. Revenue 3yr CAGR is -14% purely because FY2022 (the start year) was a one-off Brent/LNG price spike following Russia's invasion of Ukraine (EBITDA margin also jumped to 66% from 55% the prior year on the same spike); FCF 3yr CAGR of -36% mixes that same price-spike base year against FY2025, still in the tail of the Barossa/Pikka capex supercycle (capex 40% of revenue). Equity 5yr CAGR of 16.7% is inflated by the FY2020->FY2021 balance-sheet jump (equity +$6.4bn between FY2020 and FY2021, mostly the Oil Search all-scrip merger, not organic compounding) and is not representative of sustainable ROE-driven growth. selected_growth_rate (4.0%) is a mid-horizon volume-and-cost-program-driven revenue growth proxy from the component build (see assumptions.base.growth_rates), not a historical CAGR extrapolation -- appropriate given the method file's explicit routing of cyclicals away from naive CAGR extrapolation.

base.narrative: Barossa and Pikka Phase 1 complete their ramp to plateau through FY2026-27 (management's guided 25-30% production growth by 2027 vs 2024, and 2H2026 production 20-30% above 1H2026), driving above-trend revenue growth in years 1-2 as full-year contribution replaces partial-year commissioning volumes; growth then decelerates to a low-single-digit trough in years 4-5 while Papua LNG (FID targeted Q4 2026, Santos ~21% stake) is under construction and PNG LNG legacy fields decline, before a second, smaller step-up in years 6-8 as Papua LNG and PNG LNG backfill (Agogo tie-in, oil infill drilling) reach first gas/oil around 2030-31. EBITDA margin holds at the 66-67% actually delivered every year since the FY2022 price spike (not the pre-cost-program 55% of FY2021), reflecting the structural cost-reduction program ($150m/yr recurrent savings by end-2026) and Moomba Central Optimisation (>$600m lifetime savings). Capex tapers from the FY2025/26 construction-tail level (38% of revenue) toward a ~24% sustaining level by year 4, then rises again to ~27-29% in years 5-6 as Papua LNG construction capital is spent, before settling to a ~20-21% long-run sustaining rate. No oil/LNG price re-rating is assumed despite spot Brent currently trading well above Santos's guided breakeven -- growth here is volume- and cost-driven only, treating the current elevated price environment as cyclically above, not the new mid-cycle level.

bull.narrative: Oil and LNG prices stay structurally elevated (consistent with, not a further re-rate above, the ~$100+/bbl Brent and ~$11/mmBtu LNG actually realized through 1H2026-2H2026), Papua LNG reaches FID on schedule in Q4 2026 and executes without material cost overrun, Pikka scales toward and beyond its 80,000 bbl/d gross plateau with follow-on phases, PNG LNG backfill (Agogo, infill drilling, APF tie-in) and Moomba Central Optimisation overdeliver on their targeted IRRs and cost savings, and the Australian domestic gas reservation policy remains softened/non-binding through the decade rather than forcing below-market sales. Structural cost program savings exceed the $150m/yr target as headcount and procurement optimization compound, lifting EBITDA margin toward 70%. A friendlier capital-markets and FIRB environment keeps the door open to further strategic M&A interest (a fourth approach cannot be ruled out given the pattern of three prior bids), providing a scarcity-value tailwind to the multiple the market is willing to pay, though this scenario values the standalone cash flows only and does not assume a takeout premium.

bear.narrative: Brent and Asian LNG spot prices mean-revert sharply from today's elevated levels toward or below Santos's guided $45-50/bbl all-in FCF breakeven, compressing EBITDA margin from 66-67% toward the high-50s as the low-cost operating model cushions but does not fully offset the price decline. The Australian domestic gas reservation scheme is reinstated in a stricter form (mandatory 'up to 20%' reservation actually binds from 2028 as originally proposed rather than remaining softened), forcing below-market domestic sales or third-party gas purchases that pressure GLNG export economics. Papua LNG FID slips past Q4 2026 or is scaled back amid PNG political/security disruption (a recurring risk per Santos's own disclosure), delaying the second growth leg and stranding pre-FID spend; PNG LNG legacy field decline is not fully offset by backfill projects. Elevated gearing (28% including leases) combined with weaker cash flow slows the targeted $2.5bn net debt reduction by 2030, capex is not cut as fast as revenue falls (near-term sustaining spend on existing LNG plants is largely fixed), and cash tax rate benefits partially from lower PRRT/royalty crystallization as prices fall, only partly offsetting the margin and volume damage.

scenario_narratives.base: Peak construction capex on Barossa and Pikka Phase 1 is behind Santos as both reached production in 2025-2026; FY2026-27 sees a genuine step-up in free cash flow as commissioning costs unwind and full-year volumes flow through, before a mid-horizon lull while Papua LNG is built and a second, smaller growth leg as Papua LNG and PNG LNG backfill reach first production around 2030-31. EBITDA margin holds at the 66-67% actually delivered since 2022, not the immature 55% of the pre-cost-program era. No commodity price re-rating is assumed above today's already-elevated level.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prices stay structurally elevated, Papua LNG FIDs on schedule and executes cleanly, Pikka scales beyond its 80,000 bbl/d plateau, backfill and cost-reduction programs overdeliver, and Santos's repeated status as a strategic acquisition target continues to attract inbound interest -- though this scenario values only the standalone cash flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: Oil and LNG prices mean-revert hard from today's elevated levels toward Santos's own guided breakeven, a stricter domestic gas reservation scheme binds from 2028, Papua LNG slips on PNG political/execution risk, and the low-cost operating model cushions but does not offset the margin and volume damage, while capex stays comparatively sticky and de-gearing stalls.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held slightly above the 15% house default (25%) because Santos is a high-operating-leverage commodity cyclical -- management's own disclosure that every $10/bbl move in Brent swings FCF by $550-600m once plateau is reached cuts both ways, and today's spot Brent (~$100-108/bbl) sits well above the $45-50/bbl guided breakeven, meaning a mean-reversion bear case is a live, not remote, risk rather than a tail scenario. Bull weight trimmed symmetrically to 25% (from the 35% default) because the bull case requires several largely independent things to go right simultaneously (Papua LNG FID and execution, Pikka scaling past plateau, domestic gas policy staying benign, cost programs overdelivering) rather than one dominant lever. Base retained at 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Santos is valued as a mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF: reported free cash flow over FY2023-2025 is deeply depressed by the tail of the Barossa LNG and Pikka Phase 1 (Alaska) construction supercycle (capex ran 32-45% of revenue against high-60s% EBITDA margins), and FY2022's apparent FCF peak ($2.85bn) was itself a one-off oil/LNG price spike, not a repeatable base -- so neither year is extrapolated forward. Instead the model builds a component path (EBITDA margin, capex%, D&A%, cash tax rate) anchored to management's own FY2026 guidance and stated medium-term targets (25-30% production growth by 2027 vs 2024, capex guidance ~$1.95-2.15bn, unit cost trending toward $6.78/boe and below), assuming no further re-rating of an already-elevated commodity price environment. Net debt is taken inclusive of lease liabilities (management's own definition, which spiked on recognition of the Barossa FPSO lease) at the latest, 30-Jun-2026, balance date. The 2025 XRG/ADNOC-led consortium takeover approach (~US$5.76/share indicative) was formally withdrawn in September 2025 and is not live; it is noted as context for the market's demonstrated willingness to pay a strategic-scarcity premium for Santos's LNG infrastructure position, which a pure standalone-cash-flow DCF does not capture.
key_risks_to_valuation: Direct, high-magnitude exposure to Brent/JCC oil and Asian LNG spot prices with no structural hedge against a sustained downturn -- management's own sensitivity is $550-600m FCF per $10/bbl once Barossa/Pikka reach plateau, and today's spot price sits well above the guided breakeven

Papua LNG FID (targeted Q4 2026) and subsequent ~US$14bn multi-partner construction execution risk, concentrated in PNG's higher political/security-risk jurisdiction alongside existing PNG LNG exposure

Australian domestic gas reservation policy remains a live regulatory overhang even after being softened (start delayed to 2028, 'up to' 20%) -- a stricter reinstated form could force below-market domestic sales

Elevated gearing (28.1% including leases at 1H2026, $5.8-6.2bn net debt) constrains near-term capital flexibility until the targeted $2.5bn de-gearing by 2030 materialises, which itself depends on the price and volume assumptions above

No commodity price-deck re-rating is modelled -- if oil/LNG prices structurally re-rate higher (or lower) from today's already-elevated level for reasons beyond Santos's guided sensitivity, the mid-cycle component build will understate (or overstate) value versus a full price-deck model
